summary: At the Feast of Tabernacles, Jesus goes up quietly, then teaches openly in the temple, invites the thirsty to come to Him, and divides both crowd and council.
key_insight: Everyone in this chapter argues about where Jesus comes from: Galilee, Bethlehem, or a place no one knows. Jesus gives His own answer: “I am from Him, and He sent Me.” The real question is not His hometown but His Father.
story: After these things Jesus stayed in Galilee, because the leaders in Judea sought to kill Him. When the Feast of Tabernacles was near, His brothers urged Him to go to Judea and show Himself openly: “If You do these things, show Yourself to the world.” For even His brothers did not believe in Him.

Jesus answered, “My time has not yet come, but your time is always ready. The world cannot hate you, but it hates Me because I testify of it that its works are evil.” He told them to go up without Him, and He remained in Galilee. But after His brothers had gone up, He also went up to the feast, not openly, but as it were in secret.
At the feast people were asking, “Where is He?” Some said, “He is good”; others said, “No, on the contrary, He deceives the people.” Yet no one spoke openly of Him for fear of the leaders.

About the middle of the feast Jesus went up into the temple and taught. The leaders marveled, “How does this Man know letters, having never studied?” Jesus answered, “My doctrine is not Mine, but His who sent Me.” He reminded them that they circumcised a man on the Sabbath, yet were angry with Him for making a man completely well on the Sabbath. “Do not judge according to appearance, but judge with righteous judgment.”

Some from Jerusalem said they knew where this Man was from, but when the Christ came, no one would know. Jesus cried out in the temple, “You both know Me, and you know where I am from; and I have not come of Myself, but He who sent Me is true, whom you do not know. But I know Him, for I am from Him, and He sent Me.” They tried to seize Him, but no one laid a hand on Him, because His hour had not yet come. Many believed in Him, and the chief priests and Pharisees sent officers to take Him.

On the last day, that great day of the feast, Jesus stood and cried out, saying, “If anyone thirsts, let him come to Me and drink. He who believes in Me, as the Scripture has said, out of his heart will flow rivers of living water.” He spoke of the Spirit, whom those who believed in Him would receive once He was glorified.

The crowd was divided. Some said, “Truly this is the Prophet.” Others said, “This is the Christ.” Still others objected that the Christ must come from David’s line and from Bethlehem, not from Galilee. The officers returned without Him and said, “No man ever spoke like this Man!” When Nicodemus, one of the rulers, asked, “Does our law judge a man before it hears him and knows what he is doing?”, they answered, “Are you also from Galilee? Search and look, for no prophet has arisen out of Galilee.”

fit.question: Jesus told His brothers, “I am not yet going up to this feast,” and then went up after they left. Did He change His mind or mislead them?

points.label: Not on their terms
points.text: The brothers wanted Him to go up publicly and “show Yourself to the world.” Jesus refused to go that way or at their urging. When He did go, it was “not openly, but as it were in secret.”

points.label: “Not yet”
points.text: The NKJV, with many manuscripts, reads “not yet,” and Jesus gives His reason: “My time has not yet fully come.” Some manuscripts lack the word yet, but either way Jesus refuses the brothers’ plan of a public display, not the feast itself.

fit.note: Jesus declined to make the public show His brothers urged; going up quietly later fits exactly what He said.
fit.short: Jesus refused His brothers’ plan of a public display. He went up later, quietly, on the Father’s timing rather than theirs.

scene.label: The Feast of Tabernacles
scene.text: Held in early autumn after the harvest, for seven days with an eighth day of assembly (Leviticus 23:33–43). Families lived in booths made of branches to remember Israel’s years in the wilderness. It was the most joyful of the pilgrim feasts, and Jerusalem was packed.

scene.label: Water from Siloam
scene.text: The Mishnah, written down about AD 200, describes a priest drawing water from the Pool of Siloam in a golden pitcher each morning of the feast and pouring it out at the altar amid great rejoicing. Later Jewish writers linked the rite to Isaiah 12:3: “with joy you will draw water from the wells of salvation.”

scene.label: The last day
scene.text: Scholars differ on whether this was the seventh day, the climax of the water ceremony, or the eighth day of solemn assembly. Either way, Jesus’ cry came at the height of a feast that celebrated God’s gift of water.

scene.label: Out of Galilee
scene.text: The crowd knew Jesus only as a man from Nazareth in Galilee; Matthew and Luke tell of His birth in Bethlehem. The rulers’ claim was not even accurate: the prophet Jonah came from Gath Hepher in Galilee, a few miles from Nazareth (2 Kings 14:25).

scene.label: His brothers
scene.text: Mark 6:3 names them: James, Joses, Judas and Simon. They did not believe now, but after the resurrection they were with the disciples in prayer (Acts 1:14), and James became a leader of the church in Jerusalem.

witnesses.john: John alone tells this visit. His Gospel follows Jesus to Jerusalem for the feasts, and here, at a feast of water, Jesus offers living water, as He did to the Samaritan woman (4:10). John explains the saying for his readers: it spoke of the Spirit, not yet given because Jesus was not yet glorified.

seeing.reveals: Jesus speaks as the One sent from the Father, with teaching that is not His own but God’s. Standing in the temple at the height of the feast, He offers Himself as the source of the Spirit’s living water.
seeing.living: Jesus’ invitation is open: anyone who thirsts may come to Him and drink. Bring Him the thirst that religious activity has not satisfied, and let His life flow through you to others. When opinions about Him divide the room, do what Nicodemus urged: hear Him before you judge.
seeing.ponder: What are you thirsty for, and have you brought that thirst to Jesus Himself?

preaching.big_idea: Jesus offers living water to anyone who thirsts, and no one can stay neutral about Him.
preaching.watch_for: Watch the arguments about origins: Galilee, Bethlehem, “no one knows” (7:27, 41–42, 52). John lets every opinion speak, and Jesus’ own answer stands in the middle of the chapter: “I am from Him, and He sent Me” (7:29).
